title: Spark Savings competes on scale and liquidity availability, not only on headline yield
content:
A.6.1.1.1.1 defines Spark Savings as enabling "stablecoin holders to earn the best risk-adjusted rate in DeFi, **at large scale, with minimal liquidity constraints**."

The qualifiers carry the claim. Most high-yield DeFi products fail on one of the two: the rate collapses as deposits grow (yield was a function of a small opportunity, or of emissions), or capital is locked or subject to withdrawal queues so the quoted rate is not actually redeemable on demand. Spark Savings commits to all three properties simultaneously — rate quality, capacity, and redeemability.

This is only achievable because the underlying return comes from the collateral deployment mandate rather than from a bounded arbitrage or a token emission schedule: an issuer-backed reserve strategy scales with the size of the reserve.

The implication is a hard operational obligation rather than a product feature. Promising minimal liquidity constraints at large scale means the Spark Liquidity Layer must hold enough readily withdrawable assets to honour redemptions, which directly constrains how much of the balance sheet can chase the highest returns. This tension between yield and instant redeemability is what the Liquidity Layer's operational parameters exist to manage.
description: The stated target is the best risk-adjusted rate 'at large scale, with minimal liquidity constraints' — three constraints together, since high yields that break at size are the normal DeFi failure.
